regions.region: title block and central graphical abstract
regions.finding: Generic Pd(dba)2/DPEphos decarboxylative transformation of an R-group allenyl 3-oxoalkanoate to a 3,4-allenyl ketone with CO2 byproduct; classified as a general scheme, not an individual batch.
Motivation and cited prior uses/syntheses of allenyl ketones; no new experiment with a complete batch identity is reported in this region.

unresolved: The graphical abstract uses generic R1/R2 groups and gives no batch scale, duration, or yield.
Cited introduction statements were not expanded into experiments of this paper.

regions.finding: The top arrow is a ref 11 literature example; the remaining network is the authors' proposed alpha-methylene pi-allylpalladium/decarboxylation pathway. These are classified separately as literature example and mechanism.

Narrative corroborates Table 1 outcomes, including failure to afford 2a or 3a in entry 1, 33% isolated 2a in entry 5, 59% isolated 2a and 17% NMR 4a in entry 10, and no observed 3a for the DPEphos case.

Ten catalyst/ligand optimization rows extracted independently with 1a scale, catalyst/ligand loadings, THF volume, argon, temperature, time, NMR/isolated yields, qualitative complicated results, upper bounds, and table-dash markers. Entry 10 is the same experiment repeated as Table 2 entry 1 and is not duplicated.

unresolved: Table 1 does not provide workup or purification details, and several complicated/dash outcomes do not define individual product quantities.
Generic Scheme 1 structures and proposed intermediates remain unverified.

regions.finding: Eleven solvent optimization rows inspected. Table 2 entry 1 was merged with identical Table 1 entry 10; entries 2–11 are separate records, including the 25 °C footnote override for entry 11 and separate NMR versus parenthesized isolated yields.
Five substrate-scope rows extracted independently; the 1 g scale footnote for entry 2 overrides the shared 0.4 mmol scale, and the approximately 1:1 diastereomer ratios for 2a–2c are retained.
Five 2-allylic-substituted scope rows extracted independently; entry 3 uses the THF footnote override, and approximately 1:1 diastereomer ratios are retained for 2e–2g.
Two separate arrows extracted: 1j to allenyne 2j in THF (45%) and 1k to bisallene 2k in t-BuOH (67%, approximately 1:1 diastereomers), with their displayed times and catalyst loadings.

unresolved: Main-text tables and Scheme 2 omit workup and purification; Scheme 2 also omits scale, solvent volume, and atmosphere.
Most R-group-derived substrate/product structures and all stereochemical assignments remain machine-unverified.

regions.finding: One reaction of 1l furnished two products: monoallenylation product 2l (41% isolated) and diallenylation product 2m (27% isolated); both product-specific yields are linked to the same experiment.
Substrates 1m, 1n, and 1o were inspected as three distinct failed scope trials; each reaction was described as complicated and failed to afford its corresponding decarboxylation product.
Three separate cyclic-substrate arrows extracted: 1p to 2n (71%), 1q to 2o (74%), and 1r to 2p (71%), retaining displayed catalyst/ligand loadings, solvent, temperature, and times.

regions.region: lower columns conclusion, acknowledgments, and Supporting Information notice
regions.finding: Conclusion summarizes the method and the notice says analytical data are available as Supporting Information. No SI file was supplied or explicitly associated, so no SI experiment was imported.

unresolved: Figure 1 does not report the exact conditions or expected product identifiers for the three failed substrates.
Equation (1) and Scheme 3 omit scale, solvent volume, atmosphere, workup, and purification.
The Supporting Information association remains unestablished.
